subject: Where request/response artifacts are stored and how they're purged
messages:
From: Jamie Porter <jamie.porter@acme-analytics.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick question on default log retention for prompts/outputs

Hi Sean,

We're evaluating Redwood for a production integration and a few compliance folks asked for straightforward answers about what you keep by default. Two quick questions:

1) For the hosted Redwood API, what is the default retention window for request/response artifacts (prompts, model outputs, and any intermediary logs used for debugging)?
2) Where are those artifacts physically stored (region + whether backups exist) and how does deletion actually work when a customer asks for data to be deleted?

Can you point me to any short KB or a one-pager we can hand to our security reviewer? If this is easier over a quick call, I'm available tomorrow morning PST.

Thanks,
Jamie Porter
Head of Security
Acme Analytics
security@acme-analytics.com

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Jamie Porter <jamie.porter@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2028-04-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on default log retention for prompts/outputs

Hi Jamie — thanks for the clear questions. Quick high-level answers below; I pulled in our privacy lead for specifics and a short summary PDF.

High-level:
- Hosted API (default): request/response artifacts (raw prompts and model outputs) are retained for 30 days by default for debugging, billing reconciliation, and quality monitoring.
- Dedicated: retention is configurable by customer; default deployments we provision for Dedicated do not persist user prompts/outputs at the Redwood control plane unless the customer opts in (we can confirm per-customer config).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Redwood does not collect prompts/outputs to our control plane by default; logs stay in the customer's environment unless the customer configures remote telemetry.

I'll attach a short retention summary and loop in Marissa (privacy) to confirm backup/TTL behavior and deletion mechanics. If you'd like the SOC2 artifact, I can send a link once Marissa confirms which documents are shareable.

Would you like a 20-minute call tomorrow at 9:30am PST?

Best,
Sean Gallagher

Sean — thanks for looping me in. Below are the concrete details we typically give customers; I kept the language customer-facing and flagged a couple of exceptions where legal/contract language is required. Attaching a one-page summary (retention-summary.pdf).

Customer-facing defaults (Hosted API):
- Prompts & Outputs: persisted for 30 days by default. These are used for debugging, incident investigation, billing reconciliations, and quality regressions. After 30 days items are removed from the primary telemetry store and made unavailable through the console/API.
- Short-term debug artifacts (traces, expanded model traces): retained up to 90 days by default, but these are smaller slices and rotated more aggressively.
- Aggregate metrics & telemetry (latency histograms, token counts) are retained longer for trend analysis (12 months) but those are aggregated and do not contain raw prompt text.

Residency & backups:
- Data is stored in the region tied to the customer's account (e.g., us-west1 for US customers, eu-central1 for EU customers). Backups for disaster recovery are replicated within the same region set (not cross-region by default) and use the same retention policy.

Deletion mechanics:
- Primary deletion: when retention TTL expires (automated TTL), items are removed from the live store and are no longer accessible via APIs or the console.
- Manual deletion requests: customers can request immediate deletion via the support portal (SUP-4321). We escalate to the Data Ops team who trigger a deletion workflow; primary store deletion is immediate in practice (within hours).
- Backups & snapshots: we retain backups for a limited window to support restore scenarios; those backups are purged on a rolling schedule (typically within 30–60 days after the data is removed from primary). We can contractually shorten backup windows for enterprise customers.

Exemptions & notes:
- Legal holds / audit requests: if a contractual/legal obligation requires retention, we will inform the customer and follow the process in the agreement; this can override default TTLs.
- Dedicated & Private: as noted, Dedicated customers can opt to disable prompt/output persistence at provisioning. Private (VPC/on-prem) customers control telemetry collection — Redwood does not pull prompts/outputs into our control plane unless explicitly configured.
- Redaction: customers may choose to use prompt redaction at the SDK or use our built-in masking helpers. We do not automatically redact prompts.

Operational points for internal teams:
- If a customer requests immediate deletion, open SUP-4321 and tag DataOps; include account region and the specific timeframe to be deleted.
- For SOC2 evidence: provide the retention-summary.pdf plus the redaction and deletion runbook. I'll confirm which SOC2 artifacts are shareable and attach a link.

Attachment: retention-summary.pdf (one-page customer-facing summary)

Marissa Cole
Privacy & Compliance Lead
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Hi Jamie — following up with the specifics and a short summary attached. TL;DR answers below and next steps.

TL;DR for security review:
- Hosted API: prompts & model outputs retained 30 days by default; debug traces up to 90 days; aggregated metrics 12 months (no raw text).
- Residency: data kept in the account region (US/EU/APAC) with backups replicated within that region set; we do not cross-replicate outside the region by default.
- Deletion: automated TTL removes data from the primary store when it expires; manual deletions via support (SUP-4321) trigger an immediate deletion workflow; backups are purged on a rolling schedule (typically 30–60 days).

What we can provide now:
